findings.expected: T-007: "a polling fallback when SSE is unavailable" must stand in for the SSE terminal event — i.e. keep polling GET /api/atlas until the scan actually completes, then swap in the fresh snapshot.
findings.found: The interval callback calls setScanning(false) on the FIRST resolved poll regardless of whether the scan finished. setScanning(false) makes the effect's guard at line 133 (`if (!scanning) return`) re-run and clearInterval fire, so the fallback polls EXACTLY ONCE, 1500 ms after rescan(), and then stops forever. A real scan of ~/Projects takes 4620 ms (measured: `node -e "import('./server/scan.js').then(async({scan})=>{const t=Date.now();const s=await scan(require('os').homedir()+'/Projects');console.log(Date.now()-t,'ms',s.repos.length)})"` -> "real scan of ~/Projects took 4620 ms for 39 repos"). The single poll at 1500 ms therefore returns the OLD cached snapshot; the fresh one never reaches the UI and the user must reload the page. hooks.test.tsx:142-177 asserts less than the criterion demands: it queues one mock response containing already-fresh data at the first tick and then asserts scanning === 'false' (line 176), locking the defect in instead of catching it.

findings.expected: T-005: "SSE stream ends with a terminal done event" — after a scan completes the client should settle: one terminal done, one refetch, then quiet until the next POST /api/rescan.
findings.found: handleScanEvents replays the full retained `state.events` (which still contains the previous scan's terminal 'done') to EVERY new subscriber and then closes the stream with res.end() at line 225 on a 200 text/event-stream response. Per the EventSource spec a server-closed 200 stream is auto-reconnected by the client, and useAtlas.ts:110-124 keeps its single subscription alive for the app's lifetime and never closes it. Result: after ONE completed scan the browser reconnects every ~3 s forever, each time replaying start -> setScanning(true), repo -> setScanning(true), done -> setScanning(false) + fetchSnapshot(), i.e. an unbounded loop of /api/scan-events connections, /api/atlas refetches, and scanning-state flapping that disables the ScanBar Rescan button. Measured with a real EventSource client: 4 terminal 'done' events in 12 s from one scan, no rescan requested. No test covers reconnect — server/index.test.js uses fetch() (which never reconnects) and hooks.test.tsx uses a hand-driven mock transport, so the shipped EventSource path is entirely untested.

findings.expected: T-005: the SSE stream ends with a terminal done event after which /api/atlas serves fresh data; when no scan is running the client should not be told a scan just finished.
findings.found: handleScanEvents replays state.events (never cleared after a scan — only reset at startScan, index.js:150) to every new subscriber and then res.end()s when not scanning (index.js:224). A browser EventSource treats a server-closed stream as a dropped connection and reconnects (~3 s), so every reconnect re-delivers start + N repo + done for the LAST completed scan; useAtlas.ts:117-119 reacts to each replayed 'done' by setting scanning true→false and issuing a full GET /api/atlas. Result: with no scan running, the SPA re-downloads the whole snapshot (160 KB against the live ~/Projects cache) and re-runs phantom scan-progress state every few seconds for as long as the tab is open, and ScanBar (role=status, aria-live=polite, disabled={scanning}) flickers through 'Surveying n/total' each cycle.

findings.expected: T-005: after the terminal done event, /api/atlas serves the FRESH data without a restart. state.latest must only ever move forward.
findings.found: Two unsequenced writers race on state.latest: the cache seed at line 120 (`if (cached) state.latest = cached`) and the scan landing at line 170 (`state.latest = snapshot`). The boot path in the main entry calls server.triggerRescan() synchronously right after createServer(), while loadCache() is still pending, so whichever settles LAST wins. When the cache read finishes after the scan, the stale on-disk snapshot silently overwrites the fresh one and /api/atlas serves stale data indefinitely — even though the SSE stream already emitted its terminal 'done'. Reproduced deterministically with a large cache file and a fast scanFn: /api/atlas returned generatedAt '2020-01-01T00:00:00.000Z' where 'FRESH-2026' was expected. No test exercises boot-scan-vs-cache-seed ordering.
